    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    AbstractPanelElement
    Base of MenuKit's own elements: built once by a builder, immutable after.
    AbstractPanelElement.Builder<E,B>
    The builder every MenuKit element's builder extends: the shared vocabulary, in one place, with the same names everywhere.
    AlertDialog
    Builds a modal dialog with one acknowledge button.
    AlertDialog.Builder
    Builder for an AlertDialog Panel.
    Anchor
    A rectangle a library names and supplies per screen, for panels to be placed around with an AnchorPanelAdapter: a slot group's box (SlotKit), the pause menu's button column, the title screen's buttons.
    AnchorPanelAdapter
    Places a Panel on Anchors: rectangles another library names and supplies per screen (a slot group's box, the pause menu's button column).
    Attachment
    The screen a container's children are attached to, so a child added after build attaches the way a child present at the screen's init did (7.3.0).
    Button
    An interactive button within a Panel: a raised background with a centered label, an icon, or a consumer sprite as its whole face.
    Button.Builder
     
    Button.Look
    The look this frame, handed to the render hooks.
    Checkbox
    A boolean setting as a small square with a check mark and a label beside it: the settings-screen convention, and a lens onto the consumer's boolean.
    Checkbox.Builder
     
    ChildDispatch
    The one way a list of elements is rendered and receives input.
    Click
    A mouse click as seen by a PanelElement: which button, plus the modifier keys held at the moment the click was dispatched.
    ColorField
    A color setting: a swatch showing the color, and a lens onto it.
    ColorField.Builder
    Builds a ColorField.
    Column
    Lays elements out top to bottom, the vertical counterpart of Row: it positions each child with even spacing and a horizontal alignment, and returns a flat list of positioned PanelElements.
    Column.Builder
    Builds one column.
    ConfirmDialog
    Builds a modal confirm/cancel dialog.
    ConfirmDialog.Builder
    Builder for a ConfirmDialog Panel.
    ContainerRegion
    The container region (7.4.0): on a container screen, the player's inventory never scrolls, and everything above it is one column that scrolls together.
    ContainerRegion.Builder
    Builds one section of the container region.
    ContainerRegion.Sections<K>
    Builds one kind of section made per live key.
    ContainerRegion.Source
    Where a section's items are: the container it shows.
    ContainerTabs
    Tabs on the container screen's panels (7.4.0): a row of tabs, like the creative inventory's, on an edge of the container region's container list or inventory panel.
    ContainerTabs.Builder
    Builds one tab.
    ContainerTabs.Edge
    The panel edge a tab's row stands on.
    ContainerTabs.Groups<G,K>
    Builds a list of groups (ContainerTabs.groups(String, ModeScope, Supplier, Function)).
    ContainerTabs.GroupTab<G,K>
    What a list of groups' sub-tab is (ContainerTabs.Groups.tab): its group, its key, and the builder to set up.
    ContainerTabs.Icon
    What a tab's icon draws: the mod's own drawing, every frame, in the icon box at (x, y), width by height.
    ContainerTabs.Keyed<K>
    Builds a keyed list of tabs (ContainerTabs.keyed(String, ModeScope, Supplier)).
    Contribution
    One mod's part of a shared panel (SharedPanels, 7.4.0): its elements, its order in the panel, the mode it shows in and its own visibleWhen, plus the panel's own declaration (where it goes per mode, its style, its axis and gap, whether it is fixed, how many fit in a column per mode).
    Contribution.Builder
    Builds a Contribution.
    CrossAlign
    Cross-axis alignment for Row and Column.
    Declarations
    Declarations freeze; state does not.
    Divider
    A line between sections of a panel: a solid fill, no texture, no input.
    Divider.Builder
     
    Dropdown<T>
    A single-selection dropdown: a trigger showing the current choice, and a popover list to pick another from.
    Dropdown.Builder<T>
     
    DropdownMulti<T>
    A multi-selection dropdown: a trigger summarizing the chosen set, and a popover list where each row toggles its item.
    DropdownMulti.Builder<T>
     
    Easing
    An easing curve (7.4.0): eased progress for a linear progress t, both from 0 to 1.
    EditDialog
    Builds a modal dialog that edits a copy of something and writes it back only on Save (7.3.0): a title, your controls, Cancel and Save.
    EditDialog.Builder
    Builder for an EditDialog Panel.
    ElementConstants
    The colors and spacings MenuKit's elements share.
    ElementSpec
    An element whose position a layout helper (Row, Column) computes: its size now, the element itself when ElementSpec.at(int, int) is called with the computed position.
    Flow
    A run of elements laid out left to right at the panel's runtime width, wrapping onto new rows when it runs out of room: the runtime row.
    Flow.Builder
     
    Focus
    Focus for widgets MenuKit places on a screen, and the "is this point covered by MenuKit" checks.
    HudCycleStrip
    The cycle strip: a small hotbar drawn just right of the vanilla one, showing a ring of stacks that cycles through the held hotbar slot, with a spring slide each time the ring turns (since 7.1.0).
    HudCycleStrip.Axis
    Which way a ring reads on screen.
    HudCycleStrip.Direction
    Which way a ring turned.
    HudCycleStrip.SlideStart
    A slide's start, from HudCycleStrip.begin().
    HudCycleStrip.Source
    What a mod registers: the ring it would draw for a hotbar slot, if any.
    HudCycleStrip.View
    One ring, as a source sees it now.
    HudIcon
    A HUD element that draws a sprite from the GUI atlas at a given size, using vanilla's blitSprite.
    HudNotification
    A timed HUD popup that slides in, stays for a while, then fades out.
    HudNotification.Builder
     
    HudNotification.SlideDirection
    Direction the notification slides in from.
    HudPanel
    Builds HUD panels: panels drawn on the game's heads-up display.
    HudPanel.BarBuilder
    Configures a progress bar element.
    HudPanel.Builder
     
    HudPanel.ItemBuilder
    Configures an item display element.
    HudPanel.SlotBuilder
    Configures a HUD slot element.
    HudPanel.TextBuilder
    Configures a text element.
    HudSlot
    A HUD element that draws an item in a hotbar slot.
    Icon
    A picture at a fixed size: the "show a picture" primitive.
    Icon.Builder
     
    InfoBox
    A block of text on a raised background: an explanation or a notice inside a panel.
    InfoBox.Builder
     
    InputContext
    Input-time context passed to every PanelElement input method, the input twin of RenderContext: where the element's containing content origin is on screen, where the mouse is, and whether the element's surroundings are disabled.
    InsideRegion
    A region on a reference rectangle: one of nine spots, the four corners, the four edge midpoints, and the center, inset from the edge.
    ItemAnimation
    How an item draws at a point in an animation (7.4.0): given the item, its 16 px box and the animation's progress t, from 0 to 1, it draws the item.
    ItemAnimation.Frame
    An animation at one point: animation drawn t of the way through.
    ItemAnimation.Pose
    How big an item draws, about its box's center (1 is as it is), and how far it moves, in GUI pixels.
    ItemAnimation.Posing
    The ItemAnimation.Pose at each point of an animation.
    ItemDisplay
    An item drawn at a fixed size, with its count and durability bar, and optionally a colored outline.
    ItemDisplay.Builder
     
    ItemMatch
    An item rule: a stack and how another stack has to match it.
    ItemMatch.Match
    How a stack is compared with a rule's.
    ItemPicker
    A setting whose value is an item, or a list of items: slots showing the items the setting is about, and a lens onto them.
    ItemPicker.Box
    Something the dialog draws, x, y, w, h in its content's coordinates, and the box px, py, pw, ph it must stay inside.
    ItemPicker.Builder
    Builds an ItemPicker.
    ListView<T>
    A list whose rows follow the consumer's data while the screen is open (7.3.0): one row element per item, added, removed and reordered as the items change, each row kept for as long as its item's key is in the list.
    ListView.Builder<T,K>
    Builds a ListView.
    ListView.Sort
    The sort in use (7.3.0): which ListView.Builder.sort(Component, Comparator) option, in the order they were given, and whether it runs backwards.
    MenuButton
    A button that opens a menu of actions (7.3.0): a row's "more" button, with Duplicate and Delete in it.
    MenuButton.Action
    One row of the menu: its label, what it does, and whether it destroys something.
    MenuButton.Builder
    PopoverControl.Builder.size(int, int) and at least one action are required; MenuButton.Builder.label(Component) is the trigger's text.
    MK
    Mod entry point for MenuKit and the process-wide facade for HUD panels, notifications, and the recipe-book query.
    MKScreen
    Base class for standalone screens built with MenuKit: full-screen, client-local, interactive UIs not tied to a container menu.
    MKTooltip
    The one place a hover tooltip is queued: every element tooltip and the panel tooltip go through MKTooltip.queue(GuiGraphicsExtractor, Component, int, int) instead of calling vanilla's setTooltipForNextFrame directly.
    MKTooltip.Kind
    What a tooltip shows, as MKTooltip.hideWhen(Predicate) sees it.
    MKTooltip.Wheel
    Listener for MKTooltip.onWheel(MKTooltip.Wheel).
    ModeScope
    Which game mode a declaration is for (7.4.0): ModeScope.SURVIVAL, ModeScope.CREATIVE or ModeScope.BOTH.
    OutsideRegion
    A region outside a reference rectangle: pick a side, pick which end to align to, and stack away from that end.
    OwnHost
    The panel host of a library's own screen: a screen class a library ships (a custom container screen, say) that lays out its own panels the way MKScreen does, with the main panel as the frame, and joins MenuKit's claims, modals and draw order with them.
    OwnHost.Decoration
    Drawn after a panel's background and before its elements (slot frames, say).
    OwnHost.Layout
    One frame's placements, bottom to top, and the main panel's rectangle (the screen's leftPos, topPos, imageWidth, imageHeight), or null when the screen has no shown main panel.
    OwnHost.Placement
    Where a panel landed this frame: its outer rectangle, padding included, in screen coordinates.
    OwnHost.SlotOwnership
    Whether panel presents the live slot under the point (its claim then routes the point to that slot).
    OwnHost.TitleBand
    Where the screen's title sits, which decides the room reserved for it.
    Panel
    The basic unit of composition.
    Panel.Builder
    Builds a Panel.
    PanelElement
    A visual or interactive element within a Panel.
    PanelPosition
    Where a panel sits: the one placement declaration every host reads.
    PanelPosition.Mode
    How a panel is positioned.
    PanelStyle
    Visual style for a panel's background.
    Placement
    Where a panel goes in one mode (7.4.0): what it is placed against, and its position there.
    ProgressBar
    A bar filled to a fraction, read every frame: health, progress, a timer.
    ProgressBar.Builder
     
    ProgressBar.Direction
    Which way the fill grows.
    Radio<T>
    One choice of a single-selection set: a round button with a dot when its value is the RadioGroup's selection, and a label beside it.
    Radio.Builder<T>
     
    RadioGroup<T>
    The lens a set of Radio buttons shares: which value is selected, read from the consumer every frame and written back when the player picks another.
    Reference
    The rectangle a panel is placed against, a reference.
    RegionConstants
    The region layout constants, stacking gaps and edge insets, in one place.
    RenderContext
    Render-time context passed to every PanelElement.render(RenderContext).
    Row
    Lays elements out left to right: it positions each child with even spacing and a vertical alignment, and returns a flat list of positioned PanelElements.
    Row.Builder
    Builds one row.
    ScreenFrames
    A vanilla container screen made taller or shorter at a seam (7.4.0): its frame gains (or loses) by rows at row seam of its own layout, so screens of nearly one size can be made exactly one, and a tab row standing on their frames doesn't move as one opens in place of another.
    ScreenKind
    The look of the screen an element is on, which decides how it draws (6.1.0; renamed in 7.3.0).
    ScreenMatcher
    Which screens a registered slot (or any feature meant for every inventory screen) applies to.
    ScreenOrigin
    Screen-space top-left coordinates of a panel: what a pixel(...) placement supplies each frame, and what a panel host resolves every other placement to (RegionMath.resolveMenu / resolveInside).
    ScreenPanelAdapter
    Puts a Panel on vanilla container screens.
    ScrollContainer
    A clipped viewport over pre-positioned elements, scrolled vertically: the single primitive for "show content larger than its bounds".
    ScrollContainer.Builder
     
    Section
    A collapsible section: a header row that opens and closes the elements under it.
    Section.Builder
     
    SharedPanels
    Panels several mods share (7.4.0).
    Slider<V>
    A slider: vanilla's AbstractSliderButton, laid out and lensed by MenuKit.
    Slider.Builder<V>
     
    SlotClip
    Part of the created-slot contract, beside SlotScreenHook: a slot library tells MenuKit when an element places a slot, so the slot is clipped to what its panel shows of it (7.2.0).
    SlotDecorations
    What a mod draws on a container screen's slots (7.5.0), under the item or over it, so no mod mixes into the slot's draw.
    SlotDecorations.Decoration
    What one mod draws on a slot, and the tooltip it answers there.
    SlotHoverResult
    What SlotScreenHook.resolveHover(AbstractContainerScreen, double, double) answers for a screen point.
    SlotItemLooks
    What a slot's item draws as on a container screen (7.4.0): a mod says, per slot and per frame, which ItemAnimation the item draws with and how far through it is, and the slot draws that in place of the item.
    SlotItemLooks.Look
    What one mod draws a slot's item as.
    SlotRendering
    The recessed 18×18 slot frame for registered slots that live outside a vanilla container texture, the one piece of a created slot's presentation that is panel chrome rather than the slot itself.
    SlotScreenHook
    The plug a slot library fills so its panel-hosted slots (created slots, drawn inside MenuKit panels) take hover and clicks through MenuKit's own container-screen dispatch, without MenuKit naming a slot type.
    SlotScroll
    A grid of slots that scrolls inside its panel when it doesn't fit (7.4.0): as tall as its live rows while there is room, shorter by whole rows when there isn't, never under its minimum rows, scrolling past what shows.
    SlotScroll.Builder
    Builds a SlotScroll.
    SlotScroll.Cell
    Makes cell index: an element at (x, y) in the grid, shown while shown holds (on top of whatever hides it on its own).
    Tabs
    A tab strip and the area below it that shows the selected tab's body.
    Tabs.Align
    Where tabs sit within a row; in Tabs.Mode.SIDEBAR, where the label sits within its tab.
    Tabs.Builder
     
    Tabs.Mode
    How the strip lays out when the tabs don't fit one row.
    Tabs.Tab
    One tab: an id, a label, a body, and whether it shows.
    Tabs.TabSpec
    A tab under construction.
    Text
    Text drawing shared by MenuKit's elements: one line in a bounded width, and wrapped text.
    TextField
    A single-line text field: vanilla's EditBox, laid out and lensed by MenuKit.
    TextField.Builder
     
    TextLabel
    A line of text in a Panel, fixed or read every frame.
    TextLabel.Builder
     
    TextRole
    What a piece of text is for, so the kind of screen decides its color (6.1.0).
    Toggle
    A two-state on/off control: MenuKit's general boolean primitive, a lens onto the consumer's boolean and only a lens.
    Toggle.Builder
     
    Transition
    A timed change between two states, kept per key (7.4.0): one duration and one Easing, and for each key the mod names (a slot, a container, a tab) where that key is on its way.
    VanillaScreenPanelAdapter
    Puts a Panel on vanilla non-container screens: Options, Controls, KeyBinds, world select, the title screen, and any other Screen that is not a container screen.
    WidgetHost<W>
    Hosts a vanilla-style widget (anything that is a GuiEventListener and a Renderable) inside a panel, at the element's own rectangle.
    WidgetHost.Builder<W>
    Builds a WidgetHost.
    WidgetHost.Placer<W>
    Places a widget that is not a vanilla LayoutElement, or places one in the consumer's own way: called every frame and before every input event with the element's rectangle in screen coordinates.
    WrapsPanelAdapter
    Marks a class as a thin wrapper around ScreenPanelAdapter, VanillaScreenPanelAdapter or AnchorPanelAdapter, so PanelHost.captureCallerModId() walks past it to credit the mod that actually called the wrapper, not the library that wrote it.
